title: Point classes over a fixed base point via normalized closure
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $f:X	o S$ be any morphism of schemes, and let $s\in S$. Give $Z_s=\overline{\{s\}}$ its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme]; it is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $
u_s:N_s=Z_s^
u	o Z_s\hookrightarrow S$ be its normalization in $\kappa(s)$ [def-sc-normalization, def-weil-residue-field], and put $Y_s=X	imes_SN_s$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $V_f$ be the vanishing topos [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], with second projection $p_2:V_f	o S_{\mathrm{Et}}$. A point means a geometric morphism from $\mathbf{Set}$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Let $\mathcal P_s$ be the full subcategory of points $p$ of $V_f$ such that $p_2p$ is represented by a geometric point of $S$ whose underlying scheme point is $s$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. There is a bijection $	heta_s$ from the isomorphism classes of $\mathcal P_s$ to $|Y_s|$, compatible with their projections to $|X|$, for which
$$\exists\,(q\Rightarrow p)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad	heta_s([p])\in\overline{\{	heta_s([q])\}}\qquad(p,q\in\mathcal P_s).$$
Here the $2$-morphism is a $2$-morphism of points in $V_f$, as defined in [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and the closure on the right is Zariski closure in $Y_s$. In particular this relation is antisymmetric on isomorphism classes in $\mathcal P_s$. No finite-type hypothesis on $f$ and no finiteness hypothesis on $
u_s$ are imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-etale-topos-points-geometric] and [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], points of an oriented product $A_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}C_{\mathrm{Et}}$ are triples $(a,b,u)$ with $a$ a geometric point of $A$, $b$ a geometric point of $C$, and $u:gb\Rightarrow fa$ over $B$. In particular the points of $V_f$ with second support $s$ are exactly the triples with $b$ supported at $s$. The arrow is retained as data throughout; changing geometric representatives means transporting this whole triple.

source.place: ILO Exposé XI 1.8 and Theorem 1.4, printed pp. 172–174; Orgogozo §1, point triples.

proof.text: For triples $(a,b,u)$ and $(a',b',u')$, a $2$-morphism is precisely a pair $(\alpha:a\Rightarrow a',\beta:b\Rightarrow b')$ satisfying $f\alpha\circ u=u'\circ g\beta$. Here is the converse construction, not an extra hypothesis: on a triple-site generator $(U\to V\leftarrow W)^a$, [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] gives the fibre $a^{-1}U\times_{(gb)^{-1}V}b^{-1}W$. The inverse-image mates of $\alpha,\beta$ send a pair in the primed fibre to the pair of its component images in the unprimed fibre; the displayed equation makes it a pair in that pullback. These maps are natural in the generators. The colimit formula of [lem-trf-site-point-reconstruction-sets] extends them uniquely to all sheaves: a germ represented by $(Z,z,t)$ is sent to $(Z,\gamma_Z(z),t)$, where $\gamma_Z$ is the constructed fibre map. Naturality makes this well-defined on the colimit. Taking mates gives the desired $2$-morphism. Conversely the two projections of any $2$-morphism give this pair and equation, and the pullback formula recovers its value on every generator. An invertible pair gives an isomorphism by the same construction with the inverse pair.

source.place: ILO Exposé XI 1.4–1.8, fibre formula; Stacks sites.tex, reconstruction on site generators, through the cited reconstruction node.

proof.text: Put $H=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $E_s=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}H_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The canonical functor $\operatorname{Pt}(E_s)\to\mathcal P_s$ is an equivalence of categories. Indeed [lem-trf-etale-point-support-fibre] lifts the second coordinate of each triple to a point of $H_{\mathrm{Et}}$, giving essential surjectivity. For two such lifted triples, the same statement gives a bijection on the second-coordinate Hom-sets. Step 2 therefore gives a bijection on their compatible pairs, with exactly the same equation over $S$, which proves full faithfulness. This equivalence preserves the first projection and preserves and reflects existence of all $2$-morphisms, including noninvertible ones.

source.place: Orgogozo, proof of Lemma 8.3.2, initial restriction E′ = X oriented-over-S s, printed p. 18.

proof.text:
The Noetherian topological space $S$ is quasi-separated: an intersection of affine opens is an open subspace of a Noetherian space and is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] to $s\in S$ and the identity extension $\kappa(s)/\kappa(s)$, which has degree one. Its last clause permits taking precisely the normalization $N_s$ of the reduced closure $Z_s$ appearing in the statement; it supplies an integral morphism $\nu_s:N_s\to S$, normal integrality of $N_s$, and the generic inclusion $j:H\to N_s$ with $\nu_sj=i_s$. With $g:Y_s\to N_s$ the projection, [lem-trf-integral-middle-base-equivalence] applied to $X\to S\leftarrow N_s\leftarrow H$ gives a canonical equivalence
$$F_s=(Y_s)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{(N_s)_{\mathrm{Et}}}H_{\mathrm{Et}}\ \longrightarrow\ E_s.$$
It preserves the first projection after $Y_s\to X$. Composing with Step 3 gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Pt}(F_s)\simeq\mathcal P_s$, which preserves and reflects all $2$-morphisms. This is a topos equivalence induced by an integral change of the middle base, not an inference from a bijection of branches.

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 8.3.1 applied in the normalization paragraph of the proof of Lemma 8.3.2; normalization properties are Stacks 035I/035L, as stated by the cited existing node.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure of $\kappa(s)$ and its generic geometric point $\bar\eta$ of $N_s$ using [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique]. By [lem-trf-etale-point-support-fibre], all choices for the second coordinate in $H_{\mathrm{Et}}$ are isomorphic, so every point of $F_s$ can be represented as $(\bar y,\bar\eta,u)$. Every $y\in Y_s$ admits a geometric representative by the same algebraic-closure existence statement and [def-weil-geometric-point]. By [lem-trf-normal-generic-arrow-transitivity], there exists $u:j\bar\eta\Rightarrow g\bar y$, giving such a triple. If two triples have the same support $y$, choose an isomorphism $\alpha:\bar y\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar y'$ using [lem-trf-etale-point-support-fibre]. Transitivity gives $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_{(N_s)_{\mathrm{Et}}}(j\bar\eta)$ with $g\alpha\circ u=u'\circ\sigma$. The same-support full-faithfulness statement for the generic inclusion $j$ lifts $\sigma$ uniquely to an automorphism $\beta$ of $\bar\eta$ in $H_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Step 2 makes $(\alpha,\beta)$ an isomorphism of triples. Conversely isomorphic triples project to isomorphic geometric points, which have the same support. Thus the first projection gives a bijection from point isomorphism classes of $F_s$ to $|Y_s|$. Through Step 4 this is $\theta_s$; it is compatible with $|X|$ and independent of all representative choices.

source.place: Orgogozo, proof of Lemma 8.3.2: unique point class over each point of the normalized base change, from normal-base transitivity, printed p. 18.

proof.text: If $q\Rightarrow p$ in $\mathcal P_s$, Step 4 gives a $2$-morphism between the corresponding triples in $F_s$ and hence one between their first coordinates $\bar y_q\Rightarrow\bar y_p$. Its inverse-image mate on an open subterminal is a map from the singleton at $y_p$ to the fibre at $y_q$. Therefore every open containing $y_p$ contains $y_q$, and $y_p\in\overline{\{y_q\}}$. Conversely assume that closure relation. On an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}(C)$ containing $y_p$, it says that $y_q\in W$ and the primes in the same ring $C$ satisfy $P_q\subseteq P_p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-specialization-strict-local-lift] on $Y_s$, $\bar y_q$ lifts to the strict localization at $\bar y_p$. Its projections to pointed etale neighbourhoods send every germ $(U,\bar u,t)$ at $\bar y_p$ to $(U,\bar v,t)$ at $\bar y_q$. These natural, restriction-compatible maps on set-valued stalks define the mate of a $2$-morphism $\alpha:\bar y_q\Rightarrow\bar y_p$; the colimit formula [lem-trf-site-point-reconstruction-sets] ensures well-definedness. By [lem-trf-normal-generic-arrow-transitivity], $g\alpha\circ u_q=u_p\circ\sigma$ for an automorphism $\sigma$ of $j\bar\eta$. Lift it to $\beta$ on $H$ by [lem-trf-etale-point-support-fibre]. The pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ satisfies Step 2's commutation equation, hence gives the required $2$-morphism in $F_s$. Step 4 carries it to $q\Rightarrow p$. This proves both directions without comparing primes from different residue-field tensor rings.

source.place: Orgogozo, final normal-base order assertion in the proof of Lemma 8.3.2, printed p. 18; Stacks etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0GJ5 for the geometric lift and section-specialization for its germ map.

proof.text: If $y_p$ and $y_q$ lie in each other's singleton closures, those closures are equal. Each point is a generic point of this common irreducible closed subset. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] the generic point is unique, so $y_p=y_q$. The bijection and Step 6 therefore make the stated relation antisymmetric on point isomorphism classes.

lean.note: All geometric morphisms from sets with fixed second support, modulo natural isomorphisms of their direct images. The normalized base is the canonical relative normalization of Spec κ(s) → S, whose affine rings are the integral closures of A/p_s in κ(s), exactly the normalization of the reduced closure. Helper definitions belong to this classification. Uses the published etaleSheafEquivalence rather than duplicating site transport.
